items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: the same way Ella Fitzgerald would sing a song with the correct diction

ctx.x: When I started man, after the first couple of weeks, I said I will never make ten years doing this. So 42 years later here I am just retiring. So I taught. My father was a teacher and my grandfather and my grandmother were teachers. My sister is a teacher and my daughters. One is still a teacher. One taught for three years and she gave it up, she is now a nurse. But playing music, I started out I just wanted to be just strictly a jazz musician but like most New Orleans musicians who wanted to just play jazz you…

I draw from because that’s a part of my experiences you know. My mother sang. She wasn’t a professional singer but she sang in church, that’s how my parents met, she sang in church, he heard her sing and that was like the beginning of me. But my mother had a beautiful, lyrical sound. And it’s a funny thing about it, some years later I found out my tone, my sound on my trumpet, sort of has the same quality of her voice. And thinking about that over the years, probably when I was still in her womb that she was…
That’s a terrific story. I wonder if it might be part of the reason you were attracted to the flugelhorn also? To grab that alto—
